exports.description: Sets page-level attributes before first paint, so nothing changes once the page has painted: the reader's saved theme (`data-nz-theme` from `localStorage` key `nz-theme`: `light`, `dark` or `system`) and `data-nz-platform` (`apple` or `other`). The rules are on `themeScript`. Render it in `<head>` (`<head><ThemeScript nonce={nonce} /></head>` in a root layout), put the app's default theme on `<html>` (`data-nz-theme="system"`, or none for light), and put `suppressHydrationWarning` on `<html>`, whose attributes the script changes.

exports.description:
The script `ThemeScript` renders, for frameworks that inline it themselves (Astro: `<script is:inline set:html={themeScript} />`; Vite: a `transformIndexHtml` tag) or that allow it by hash under a strict CSP. It runs in `<head>`, before `<body>` exists, and sets two attributes on `<html>`:

- **`data-nz-theme`, the reader's saved theme.** It reads `localStorage` key `nz-theme`; when the value is `"light"`, `"dark"` or `"system"`, it sets `data-nz-theme` to that value, replacing what the server rendered (the server's value is the app's default; the stored one is the reader's choice). `"system"` is set as is, not resolved: CSS follows the operating system from it, live, with no listener. With nothing stored, any other value, or storage blocked (a sandboxed frame, disabled site data), the attribute is left as the server rendered it. A theme switch saves the choice with `localStorage.setItem('nz-theme', value)` and sets the attribute itself.
- **`data-nz-platform`**: `"apple"` when the platform string matches `/mac|iphone|ipad|ipod/i`, else `"other"`. The platform string is `navigator.userAgentData.platform` where the browser has it (Chromium: `"macOS"`, `"Windows"`, …), else `navigator.platform` (`"MacIntel"`, `"iPhone"`, `"iPad"`; iPadOS reports `"MacIntel"`, which is still Apple). It never reads the user-agent string. A value already on `<html>` (set by the server, or by a test) is kept. Kbd reads the attribute to show `⌘K` or `Ctrl+K`.

Each half runs in its own `try`, so blocked storage never stops the platform half, and the script never throws into the page.

Under a strict CSP, allow it by hash: `script-src 'sha256-nA1HUQWDdDUFqqoxWbjzCzcYSjzWLEe0pwDdRCMGqOw='`. The hash changes only when the script does, and a change is called out in the changelog.
exports.name: themeScript
